name: Jade Lantern, Tide Kept
description: A single emerald glass orb rises from the floor of a dark room at dawn, hangs high and full at noon, drifts east and widens its halo through the evening, then sinks to rest above a pool of its own light at night, while soft, barely-banded shells of jade quietly record each hour of music the house played.
listening: Bass breath swells the orb by a few percent, rising tension inflates it slightly before a drop, treble loosens the halo into haze, the key leans its highlight between mint and jade, each song re-angles the light falling on the glass, and every hour's energy is laid down as one faint luminous shell in the halo, so by midnight the glow is a portrait of the day.

curator.verdict: A single emerald glass orb with mint rim light sits squarely inside the direction, reads clearly on a coarse grid and shifts position, scale and halo across the day; it is distinct from the recent warm amber days. The concentric halo rings at 3 pm and 8 pm edge toward pattern, but they are wide and soft enough to keep the piece calm, so it hangs.
